complete_closure_policy.authority_seat_scope: one key ID and one identity/organization pair may span gaps only under one unchanged authority class
complete_closure_policy.validation_entrypoint_identity: complete_closure module, acceptance alias, package API and CLI share one immutable aggregate-bounded snapshot wrapper
complete_closure_policy.runtime_authority: supported operational entrypoints use current trusted system time and root-owned non-group/world-writable /usr/bin/openssl by absolute path under a minimal deterministic environment; caller time, executable, PATH, OpenSSL configuration, module path and dynamic-loader overrides are rejected or discarded, while the underscored fixed-clock fixture is confined to the already trusted Python process
complete_closure_policy.lexical_scope_custody: evidence, registry, key, signature and review paths retain canonical lexical names; every root, parent and final object is opened with no-follow semantics; shared ancestor directory identities are pinned across one complete validation transaction; the final visible name must still identify the opened file after reading
complete_closure_policy.contract_semantic_binding: issuer, evidence-set and reviewer digests bind the canonical SHA-256 of the complete current contract object in addition to its revision label
complete_closure_policy.committed_accepted_envelope_discovery: recursive content identity under evidence/external through filesystem-anchor and child directory descriptors, with no-follow traversal and stable lexical/opened/post-read object identity

authority_owned.closure_rule: Every authority class named for a gap signs exactly its versioned class-scoped claims. Multiple seats inside one gap use distinct key IDs and identity/organization pairs. Across a complete package, one key ID and one identity/organization pair may span gaps only under one unchanged authority class; neither may impersonate different authority roles. Every issuer and reviewer binds the canonical contract digest; every final reviewer binds the same policy, review roster and acceptance context; supported public validation owns its clock, preserves canonical lexical path identity, pins shared directory objects across the complete transaction, and executes only a verified root-owned /usr/bin/openssl under a sanitized environment independent of caller PATH or loader/configuration variables; every committed accepted envelope is discovered recursively by descriptor-anchored stable content and revalidated under an out-of-band pin; real external evidence and independent acceptance remain required.

claim_ceiling: G10 closes repository-controlled authority quorum, cross-gap role aliasing, claim-scope/version binding, canonical-contract content binding, final-review-set integrity, transaction-wide lexical filesystem custody, trusted clock and absolute cryptographic-executable custody, canonical validation-entrypoint identity, and descriptor-anchored committed accepted-envelope discovery only; it cannot manufacture E5-E7, administrative, upstream, physical, provider, vendor, independent-assurance, signing, pilot, store, or release authority.
